cleanIntro:
This guide follows Rizzini's instruction and maintenance manual for its shotguns. The book prints no model name, so check your BR110 Sporter IPS against it. Every step here is the book's general procedure, stated as generally as the book states it.

The gun comes apart in three pieces: fore-end, barrels, and the stock with the receiver. That is as far as Rizzini's disassembly goes. ⚠ The barrels never go back into the receiver with the fore-end still on them.

steps.title: Safety on: slider back, S fully showing
steps.action: This guide follows Rizzini's manual for its shotguns, which prints no model name, so check your variant against it. Point the muzzles in a safe direction and push the safety slider backwards until the letter S shows completely.
steps.prose: If any part of the S is still covered, the safety is not fully engaged. The safety is an extra measure, not a substitute for checking the chambers yourself in the next step.
steps.quote: the safety is engaged when the slider is pushed backwards and reveals the "S" letter completely.
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — SAFETY CHARACTERISTICS, printed p.10
steps.warn: Never leave the firearm unattended and always make sure it is unloaded before performing any assembly, disassembly or maintenance operations.

steps.title: Top lever across, both chambers emptied and checked
steps.action: Push the top lever (Rizzini calls it the unlocking key) to the right and open the gun. Take any shells out of both chambers, then look into each chamber yourself before you go on.
steps.prose: Open the gun where you can see where a shell lands. Do not start taking the gun apart until you have seen both chambers empty.
steps.quote: Warning: To prevent the firearm from discharging accidentally, make sure it is unloaded before disassembling it.
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO DISASSEMLE SHOTGUN, printed p.13

steps.title: Gun closed, fore-end off with its release lever
steps.action: Close the empty gun. Work the fore-end release lever and take the fore-end off the barrels.
steps.prose: The fore-end comes off first. With it still on, the barrels cannot come away from the receiver cleanly.
steps.quote: Remove the fore-end from the barrels acting on the release lever(fig.1).
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO DISASSEMLE SHOTGUN, printed p.13

steps.title: Top lever right, gun opened all the way
steps.action: Turn the top lever to the right and open the gun completely, tilting the barrels down as far as they go.
steps.prose: The barrels only come free of the hinge pins when the gun is open all the way. Half-open, they are still held.
steps.quote: Rotate the unlocking key to the right and open the firearm completely, tilting the barrels.
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO DISASSEMLE SHOTGUN, printed p.13

steps.title: Barrels lifted straight up out of the receiver
steps.action: Lift the barrels out of the receiver with a straight, vertical movement.
steps.prose: Lift, do not twist. The hinge pin housings on the barrels and the hinge pins in the receiver are what keep the gun in line, and levering them marks those surfaces.
steps.quote: Extract the barrels from the receiver with a vertical movement (Fig.2).
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO DISASSEMLE SHOTGUN, printed p.13

steps.title: Fore-end back on the barrels for safe keeping
steps.action: Put the fore-end back on the barrels, pressing gently until the two parts hold together.
steps.prose: Gentle pressure is all it takes. A loose fore-end on the bench is the part that gets knocked off and scratched.
steps.quote: Mount the fore-end back on the barrels making the two parts adhere with a gentle pressure (Fig.3).
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO DISASSEMLE SHOTGUN, printed p.13

steps.title: Top lever back to centre before the gun goes in its case
steps.action: Before storing the gun in its case, bring the top lever back to its central position: hold it pushed to the right and press its pin on the receiver face all the way down, then let the lever go.
steps.prose: With the barrels off, the lever stays over to the right until you release it this way. Rizzini recommends it before storage; it is not needed to clean the gun.
steps.aside: Once the pin has been pressed all the way down, release the key so that it can go back to its central position
steps.quote: We recommend bringing back the unlocking key to its central position before storing the firearm in its case.
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO DISASSEMLE SHOTGUN, printed p.13

steps.title: ⛔ Field strip complete: Rizzini stops here
steps.action: Fore-end, barrels, and the stock with the receiver. That is the whole disassembly Rizzini gives the owner. Taking the stock off to clean the trigger group before long storage, and the choke tubes if your barrels take them, are under DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Repairs and adjustments go to Rizzini or a gunsmith, never the bench.
steps.quote: Never attempt to modify or repair your own firearm.
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — SERVICE AND REPAIR, printed p.14

steps.title: Bores: cleaned with a cloth pull-through the same day
steps.action: At the end of every day you shoot the gun, clean the bores of both barrels with a cloth pipe cleaner.
steps.prose: Doing it every time is what keeps the bores clean enough that a metal brush is never needed.
steps.aside: Performing such cleaning consistently will spare you the need to use metal-brush pipe cleaners.
steps.quote: At the end of the day in which the firearm has been used, clean the bore of the barrels using a cloth pipe cleaner.
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CLEANING THE BARRELS, printed p.13

steps.title: Choke tubes: cleaned and oiled with the barrels
steps.action: If your barrels take choke tubes, clean and lubricate the tubes every time you clean the barrels. Look each one over for dents or deformation.
steps.prose: A dented or bent tube is not straightened. It is replaced.
steps.quote: Every time you clean the barrels, choke tubes must be cleaned and lubricated too.
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — INRECHANGEABLE CHOKES, printed p.16
steps.warn: If, for any reason, the choke tubes are deformed or show any dents, they need to be replaced

steps.title: Outside of the barrels and all metal: wiped with an oiled cloth
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the barrels and every metal part of the gun with a cloth dampened in oil, taking off every trace of dirt and sweat.
steps.prose: Sweat from your hands is what starts rust on the steel, so wipe everywhere the gun was held.
steps.quote: The external part of the barrels and every metal part of the firearm should be cleaned using a cloth dampened in Rizzini® oil, to remove every trace of dirt or sweat, which are the worst enemies to steel.
steps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CLEANING THE BARRELS, printed p.13

deepSteps.title: Long storage: the trigger group cleaned and lightly oiled
deepSteps.action: If the gun is going away for a long time, such as the end of the season, the trigger group mechanism is cleaned and given a thin layer of oil first. Use oil only, never grease.
deepSteps.prose: This is the one job Rizzini gives the owner past the field strip, and it is only for long storage.
deepSteps.quote: the trigger group mechanism needs to be cleaned and covered with a thin layer of Rizzini® oil.
deepSteps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CLEANING THE BARRELS, printed p.13
deepSteps.warn: Never use grease to perform such operation.

deepSteps.title: Stock off with Rizzini's stock key
deepSteps.action: To reach the trigger group, take the stock off using the stock key Rizzini supplies. Competition models come with it; for hunting models Rizzini supplies it separately.
deepSteps.prose: Rizzini does not describe the stock removal beyond this, and it does not describe taking the trigger group apart. If you are not sure how your stock comes off, stop here and take the gun to a gunsmith.
deepSteps.aside: For hunting models, the key is available at Rizzini®.
deepSteps.quote: To access the trigger group, remove the stock using the specific key (Fig.1) supplied with competition models.
deepSteps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CLEANING THE BARRELS, printed p.13
deepSteps.warn: Such operations can be performed by people who are familiar with firearms. If you have any doubt, ask your gunsmith.

deepSteps.title: Choke tubes: screwed in by hand, never forced
deepSteps.action: If your barrels take choke tubes, screw each tube in by hand. If one is hard to turn, do not force it: take it out and clean the barrel thread with the tool on the back of the choke key.
deepSteps.prose: Finishing with the key takes only light pressure, not strength. A tube that needs force has dirt in the thread.
deepSteps.aside: The following action with the key should not require any strength, but only a light pressure.
deepSteps.quote: Install the choke tubes manually on the barrels. Do not force if difficult.
deepSteps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — INRECHANGEABLE CHOKES, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Steel shot: check the barrel marking and the chokes
deepSteps.action: Before you shoot steel shot, check that the barrels carry the Italian proof house's steel-shot marking and that any choke tubes are marked Steel Shot. Rizzini does not recommend steel shot through 1-star (F) or 2-star (IM) tubes.
deepSteps.prose: That is the last thing the book gives the owner to check on the barrels.
deepSteps.quote: Use of steel shots is not recommended with 1-star choke tubes (F) and 2-star ones (IM).
deepSteps.cite: Rizzini Instruction and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — INRECHANGEABLE CHOKES, printed p.16
deepSteps.warn: In order to fire steel shots, the firearm must be tested and receive approval by the Italian testing authority, and receive their marking stamped in the sleeve.

cleaning.name: BARRELS
tasks: Bores of both barrels cleaned with a cloth pipe cleaner at the end of every shooting day
Done every time, a metal brush is not needed

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBES
tasks: If fitted: every tube cleaned and lubricated each time the barrels are cleaned
⛔ A deformed or dented tube is replaced, never used

cleaning.name: METAL PARTS
tasks: Outside of the barrels and every metal part wiped with an oil-dampened cloth
Every trace of dirt and sweat taken off
Never grease the trigger group; a thin layer of oil only

reassembly: Chambers checked empty before the gun goes back together.
Fore-end off the barrels first, with its release lever. ⚠ Do not try to fit the barrels to the receiver with the fore-end on.
Top lever turned to the right until it stays there.
Barrels set into the receiver with the hinge pin housings on the barrels matched to the hinge pins in the receiver.
Barrels tilted up with a smooth, even movement. When the top lever springs back, the barrels are locked to the receiver.
Fore-end mounted back on the barrels, pressed gently until it holds.
⚠ Never force the action if it sticks. Stop and find out why.
fncheck: With both chambers confirmed empty and the muzzles in a safe direction, check the barrels are locked to the receiver and the top lever has sprung back. Check the fore-end is held on the barrels. Push the safety slider back and confirm the S shows completely. If anything did not go back the way it came out, or the gun does not work properly, take it to Rizzini or a gunsmith before firing it.
